title: IAM access grid by hosting tier and SIEM export guide
content:
Purpose:
This working doc defines a compact, environment-aware IAM role grid (RBAC v2 style) and an associated SIEM/audit export contract. The goal is to provide a single reference for engineers and auditors when scoping access for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments, and to outline a minimal evidence automation implementation for compliance proofs.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: platform engineers, security, SRE, compliance owners, solutions eng.
- Scope: Identity/authorization surface for control-plane and serving-plane operations, audit event schema fields required for SOC/ISO traces, and evidence automation triggers for customer audits.
- Out of scope: full Conjur/KMS key material policies (refer to KMS-playbook).

High-level approach (novelty):
We model RBAC as a 3-axis grid instead of a flat matrix: Role (actor capability), Tenant-scope (global | tenant-scoped | host-isolated), and Assurance Level (regular | elevated-session | emergency-justified). Combining axes gives concise policies and audit signals that vary by hosting tier.

Role axis (examples):
- Viewer: read-only telemetry + config view (no token management)
- Operator: start/stop deployments, adjust autoscale policies, view logs
- ModelOps: can push model artifacts, change model version, rollback
- BillingAdmin: view/adjust billing metadata, reserve capacity
- Auditor: read-only access to audit logs, evidence bundles
- SupportEscalation: can access tenant traces for debugging after approval
- InfraAdmin: infra-level (host) admin for dedicated/private (not available in hosted tenant scope)

Tenant-scope axis by hosting tier (rules):
- Hosted (public Redwood API): default scope = tenant-scoped. No direct infra-level roles. Operators acting across multiple tenants are strictly authorized with ServicePrincipal + justification and recorded in elevated_session audit records.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): two modes depending on contract: (A) Tenant-owned control plane - infra admins can be customer-managed; (B) Redwood-managed pool - Redwood InfraAdmin has host privileges but must use segmented service principals per-customer. Audit bundling differs per mode.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): control plane is customer-managed or hybrid; Redwood support access requires explicit EAS (evidence approval step) and time-limited emergency roles.

Assurance Level axis (how to implement):
- regular: normal tokens/keys with standard rotation
- elevated-session: requires justification, MFA, short-lived token, and a named ticket id recorded in audit.record.request.context.ticketId
- emergency-justified: allowed only for InfraAdmin/SupportEscalation, requires post-hoc attestation and automatic evidence export to customer SIEM if requested

Compact role grid (CSV-like view):
Role,Allowed in hosted,Allowed in dedicated,Allowed in private,Default assurance level,Can request elevated
Viewer,yes,yes,yes,regular,no
Operator,limited(tenant ops only),yes* (see note),restricted,regular,yes
ModelOps,yes,yes,restricted,regular,yes
BillingAdmin,yes,yes,no,regular,no
Auditor,yes,yes,yes,regular,no
SupportEscalation,no,yes,yes,restricted,yes
InfraAdmin,no,conditional(see infra-mode),conditional,emergency,no

Notes:
- "limited(tenant ops only)" for hosted means operators can act only on resources tied to that tenant; cross-tenant operator activity requires a service principal and is logged as elevated-session.
- For Dedicated: infra-mode (Redwood-managed vs customer-managed) changes whether Redwood InfraAdmin is allowed. Document the contract in onboarding artifacts.

Policy template snippets (conceptual, not infra copy/paste):
- Minimal tenant-scoped policy snippet (JSON-like):
{
  "Version": "2024-01-01",
  "Statement": [
    {"Effect": "Allow", "Action": ["deploy:Describe","deploy:List"], "Resource": "arn:redwood:tenant:${tenant_id}:*"},
    {"Effect": "Deny", "Action": ["infra:*"], "Resource": "*"}
  ]
}

- Elevated-session wrapper:
{
  "Condition": {"StringEquals": {"session:assurance": "elevated", "session:ticketId": "TICKET-1234"}},
  "DurationSeconds": 900
}

Audit and SIEM export contract (core fields we require from serving + control plane):
- event_id (string, uuid)
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- actor_id (user/service principal id)
- actor_role (one of: Viewer, Operator, ModelOps, BillingAdmin, Auditor, SupportEscalation, InfraAdmin)
- actor_scope (tenant_id | host_id)
- action (string verb, e.g., DeployModel, StartInstance, RollbackModel, ExportAuditBundle)
- resource_arn (string)
- outcome (success|failure|partial)
- auth_method (api_key|oauth|service_principal|mfa_session)
- assurance (regular|elevated|emergency)
- ticket_id (optional, present for elevated/emergency)
- correlation_id (request chain id)
- evidence_refs (list of artifact ids or S3 keys)
- tenant_data_flag (true|false) — indicates whether payload contains tenant PII-sensitive fields
- export_to_siem (none|syslog|kafka|http)

Mapping guidance to SIEM fields (example for Splunk syslog JSON):
- Splunk event._time <- timestamp
- Splunk event.actor <- actor_id
- Splunk event.action <- action
- Splunk event.result <- outcome
- Splunk event.metadata.assurance <- assurance
- Splunk event.metadata.ticket <- ticket_id

Evidence automation sketch (for audit readiness):
1) Trigger points: any action with assurance != regular or any access to tenant_data_flag=true OR when a tenant requests an evidence bundle export.
2) Collector: lightweight Evidence-Agent running in control plane that: captures relevant logs, bundles config snapshots (IAM policy hashes, model version id, deployment manifest), and signs bundle with system key.
3) Upload: evidence bundles are pushed to a tenant-owned S3 (or to Redwood staging bucket with explicit ACL and TTL) and a pointer is emitted in audit.event.evidence_refs.
4) Retention: default 90 days for hosted evidence (customer export on request), 365 days for Dedicated Enterprise (configurable via contract), private per-customer policy.

SIEM export modes by hosting tier:
- Hosted: push aggregated, sanitized audit events to internal Kafka topic redwood.audit.events -> SIEM connector filters tenant_data_flag and routes metadata to corporate SIEM. For customer-facing evidence, provide signed bundles on demand.
- Dedicated: enable per-customer SIEM export (syslog/kafka/https) with customer-managed endpoint; ensure mutual TLS + token rotation. If Redwood-managed, exports are tenant-filtered by host_id.
- Private: primary model is local export; Redwood support requires explicit onboarding in SIEM contract and must use EAS.

Policy enforcement patterns (practical):
- Least-privilege by default, explicit allowing statements only for tenant-scoped ARNs.
- Deny-by-default at control-plane gateway for infra APIs in hosted mode.
- Automatic short-lived tokens for elevated sessions via token broker service; token broker requires ticket id and justification.
- Periodic automated access reviews for roles with cross-tenant privileges (monthly).

Example audit flow for an elevated operator in hosted mode:
- Operator requests elevated session via internal portal -> portal creates ticket INF-5432 -> portal calls token-broker with ticket id and obtains MFA-bound token -> token-broker issues short-lived token with session:assurance=elevated -> all requests with that token include ticket_id in audit payload -> Evidence-Agent creates bundle on first elevated action and marks export_to_siem=none by default -> Audit team can request bundle export to customer SIEM with signed URL.

Open questions / items to resolve (working list):
- Should tenant_data_flag be a tri-state (none|meta|full) instead of boolean? (Impacts sanitization policy).
- For Dedicated Redwood-managed pools, what is the canonical host_id and how do we map cross-tenant logs to a single shared export? Need infra input (see INFRA-2143).
- Emergency attic: define a post-hoc attestation workflow and SLA for attestation completion.
- Evidence encryption-at-rest key ownership for Dedicated vs Hosted (customer-managed vs Redwood-managed).

Onboarding checklist (minimum):
- Document contract mode (Redwood-managed vs customer-managed infra).
- Configure token-broker policy for elevated sessions.
- Ensure Evidence-Agent deployed in control plane and has upload path configured.
- Map SIEM export endpoints and test mutual TLS.
- Run red-team exercise to validate deny-by-default rules do not break customer flows.

Appendix: short examples and references
- Example minimal event (JSON):
{
  "event_id": "uuid-1234",
  "timestamp": "2025-01-12T18:34:22Z",
  "actor_id": "user:a.patel@redwood.com",
  "actor_role": "Operator",
  "actor_scope": "tenant:acme-corp-123",
  "action": "StartDeployment",
  "resource_arn": "arn:redwood:deployment:acme-corp-123:blue-v1",
  "outcome": "success",
  "auth_method": "mfa_session",
  "assurance": "elevated",
  "ticket_id": "INF-5432",
  "evidence_refs": ["s3://evidence-staging/tenant-acme/2025-01-12/bundle-01.tar.gz"],
  "export_to_siem": "none"
}

- Useful references and related docs:
  - Confluence: Access Patterns Overview (linked above)
  - Jira: INFRA-2143 (token broker work), SEC-708 (evidence agent work)
  - GitHub: infra PR #912 (token broker prototype)

Action items for next sprint:
- (A) Finalize schema for tenant_data_flag and ticket_id presence (owner: Aisha).
- (B) Implement Evidence-Agent prototype in staging and wire to token-broker (owner: Marco).
- (C) Draft Dedicated onboarding checklist with legal for key ownership (owner: Sofia).

Notes to reviewers: This is intentionally compact to keep adoption friction low. Comments inline or ping #security-access on Slack. We will iterate the export contract with SRE and infra team before finalizing for audits.
